en.name: Dried shrimp
en.summary: Dried shrimp are small shrimp boiled in brine and sun-dried, used a pinch at a time for savoury depth. Airtight in a cool dry cupboard they keep 4–6 months; refrigerated 6–12 months, and frozen about 12 months. Most Chinese kitchens keep them cold, and in a humid climate that is right.
en.pantry: An airtight jar in a cool, dry, dark cupboard gives about 4–6 months. That range is the general dried-food figure taken at the short end, because dried shrimp are oily and salted rather than merely dried, and no agency publishes a number for them specifically. The rule for goods that need no refrigeration is a sealed or covered container somewhere cool and dry. Check the jar often: dried shrimp that has picked up moisture goes tacky, then musty, then mouldy, and the change is quick once it starts.
en.fridge: Most Chinese kitchens keep dried shrimp in the fridge rather than the cupboard, and in a warm humid climate that is the sensible choice: about 6–12 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a well-sealed jar. It slows the oil going rancid and keeps pantry moths out. This figure is ordinary practice rather than a published one. Let the jar reach room temperature before opening so condensation does not settle inside, and never put a damp spoon in.
en.freezer: Frozen, they keep about 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F) — again ordinary practice, not a published figure. Double-bag them, because the smell transfers to everything else in the freezer with alarming efficiency. Use them straight from frozen: they are dry enough that they do not clump, and they go into the wok or the soak without thawing. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the timeline is about the oil and the aroma.
en.thawing: No thawing needed — use them straight from the freezer, or soak them in warm water as the recipe requires. Reseal the bag immediately.
spoilage: Shrimp that have gone tacky or soft instead of dry and firm.
A musty or mouldy smell rather than a sweet salty-marine one.
A sharp, paint-like rancid smell from the oil.
A dull grey-brown colour instead of pink-orange, or visible mould.
tips: Buy small quantities often; they are used a pinch at a time.
Keep them in the fridge or freezer if your kitchen is humid.
Dry spoon only — moisture is what ruins a jar.
Soak them and keep the soaking water for the dish; it is full of flavour.

faq.q: How long do dried shrimp keep?
faq.a: About 4–6 months airtight in a cool dry cupboard, 6–12 months refrigerated, and about 12 months frozen.
In a warm or humid kitchen, yes. It slows the oil going rancid and keeps insects out. In a cool dry cupboard the pantry is fine.
Yes, about 12 months at −18 °C. Double-bag them because the smell transfers, and use them straight from frozen.

faq.q: How can you tell if dried shrimp have gone bad?
faq.a: Tackiness or softness means moisture; a musty smell or mould means it has gone further; a sharp paint-like smell means the oil is rancid.

zh.name: 蝦米
zh.summary: 蝦米是小蝦用鹽水煮過後曬乾的乾貨，每次只用一小撮就能帶出鹹鮮。密封放陰涼乾燥櫥櫃可放 4～6 個月；冷藏 6～12 個月；冷凍約 12 個月。多數中式廚房會冰起來，在潮濕氣候下這是對的。
zh.pantry: 密封罐放陰涼、乾燥、避光的櫥櫃，大約可放 4～6 個月。這個區間取自乾貨通用數字的短端，因為蝦米是含油又含鹽的，而不只是曬乾而已，也沒有機構針對它公告過數字。不需冷藏的乾貨通則是密封或加蓋容器放陰涼乾燥處。請常常檢查：受潮的蝦米會先變黏、再出霉味、然後長霉，而且一開始變化就很快。
zh.fridge: 多數中式廚房把蝦米放冰箱而不是櫥櫃，在濕熱氣候下這是明智的選擇：密封罐放 4 °C 以下約 6～12 個月。冷藏可以減緩油脂氧化，也擋掉米蟲。這個數字是一般實務而非公告值。開罐前讓罐子回到室溫，避免內部結露；也絕對不要用濕湯匙挖。
zh.freezer: 冷凍的話，−18 °C 下大約 12 個月——同樣是一般實務而非公告值。請套兩層袋，因為那個味道轉移到冷凍庫其他東西上的效率高得驚人。要用時直接從冷凍取：它夠乾，不會結塊，直接下鍋或下泡水碗都可以。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，期限講的是油脂與香氣。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍——直接從冷凍取用，或照食譜用溫水泡發。取完立刻封回袋口。
spoilage: 蝦米變黏或變軟，而不是乾爽結實。
聞起來有霉味、陳味，而不是鹹鮮的海味。
油脂散發刺鼻的油漆味。
顏色由粉橘轉為暗灰褐，或看得到霉。
tips: 少量多次購買；它本來就是一次用一小撮。
廚房潮濕的話就放冷藏或冷凍。
只能用乾燥的湯匙——水氣是毀掉整罐的元兇。
泡發的水留下來一起入菜，那裡面全是味道。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼乾燥櫥櫃約 4～6 個月，冷藏 6～12 個月，冷凍約 12 個月。
濕熱的廚房建議冷藏，可以減緩油耗、避免生蟲。櫥櫃夠陰涼乾燥的話則不必。
可以，−18 °C 下約 12 個月。請套兩層袋（氣味會轉移），直接從冷凍取用。
變黏變軟代表受潮；出現霉味或長霉代表更嚴重；刺鼻油漆味代表油脂油耗。
